decisions.title: Pitch the person who owns the problem, not HR
decisions.decision: Use job ads as a buying signal and send a researched pitch to the finance or operations owner instead of 'applying' to jobs.
decisions.why: A job ad shows pain, budget and urgency; HR inboxes are the wrong buyer.
decisions.alternatives: Auto-send applications to the job ad's email.
decisions.note: Later became one use case of the wider platform (see 'Job automation becomes one use case').

decisions.title: Target higher-paid admin roles and volume hiring
decisions.decision: Focus on R18k+/month admin and finance roles and bulk hiring (e.g. call centres).
decisions.why: South African wages make one low-paid role a weak automation case.

decisions.title: Open source only, no Power BI or Qlik
decisions.decision: Build analytics without paid BI licences.
decisions.why: Cost, and everything should be code Claude Code can change.

decisions.title: Own React dashboards instead of Lightdash or Metabase
decisions.decision: Dashboards and reports are built in the platform's own React code (later ECharts).
decisions.why: A solo founder with Claude Code; Lightdash's AI features need the ~$3,000/month cloud plan; AGPL risk with Metabase.

decisions.title: Neon serverless Postgres, not Redshift
decisions.decision: Use Neon's free Postgres tier as the platform database.
decisions.why: Free, standard Postgres, scales to zero; Redshift is costly and overkill.

decisions.title: Real market data, no fake personal data
decisions.decision: Use real public data; anything simulated is labelled; no personal contact data in demos.
decisions.why: Credibility and POPIA.

decisions.title: A live public demo on real SA data
decisions.decision: Start with the SA Automation Opportunity Index on Adzuna's South Africa job feed.
decisions.why: Shows the capability on data that changes every day.

decisions.title: Host on Netlify
decisions.decision: Initial hosting choice for the site.
decisions.why: Free static hosting.
decisions.note: Replaced the same evening by GitHub Pages.

decisions.title: Host on GitHub Pages
decisions.decision: Site deployed from the repo by GitHub Actions after each refresh.
decisions.why: Free, same place as the code and the daily job.
decisions.note: Plan to move to Cloudflare Pages at launch (see production plan).

decisions.title: More jobs via AI search, with verified links
decisions.decision: Add Claude and Gemini/Google search job finders; only keep URLs that were really retrieved.
decisions.why: Free APIs alone gave too few jobs; AI search can invent links unless checked.
decisions.note: Adzuna paid plan added on 13 Nov.

decisions.title: Distinctive AI-analytics-first brand
decisions.decision: Rebrand the landing page around automated analytics with a live demo and a real identity.
decisions.why: The first version looked generic and still told the old story.

decisions.title: Neon stays the database; Sheets only as an export
decisions.decision: Google Sheets is used for the Colab job finder's output, not as the platform store.
decisions.why: Sheets can't do joins, roles or history at platform scale.
decisions.alternatives: Google Sheets as the main database.

decisions.title: Keep full job descriptions, tools and companies
decisions.decision: Store the full ad, extracted tools and skills, and the employer for later analysis.
decisions.why: These fields are what the analysis is built on.

decisions.title: Enrich only the companies that posted the jobs
decisions.decision: Company research, domains and contacts feed a private CRM for the employers in the data.
decisions.why: Keeps outreach relevant and the data lawful.
decisions.note: The job-automation CRM was replaced on 14 Nov by the sales CRM for the industry analysts.

decisions.title: Build our own analytics agent
decisions.decision: Chat → safe SQL → chart and report artifacts, with a semantic guide, instead of adopting WrenAI or Vanna.
decisions.why: Full control of branding, cost and SA datasets; Vanna was archived.

decisions.title: Model-agnostic agent harness with budgets
decisions.decision: One loop for all agents, on OpenRouter or Claude, with dollar caps, verified saves and an audit log.
decisions.why: Agents must be cheap, safe and checkable.

decisions.title: Keep multinationals operating in SA; drop firms with no SA presence
decisions.decision: Foreign firms without a South African presence leave the sales pipeline.
decisions.why: They can't buy local services; multinationals in SA can.

decisions.title: Analyst API on Render (Docker blueprint)
decisions.decision: Run the FastAPI analyst on Render's free plan.
decisions.why: Free, deploys from the repo.
decisions.note: Render Starter (~$7/month) planned for production to avoid cold starts.

decisions.title: Real PowerPoint with native charts, and direct PDF
decisions.decision: Downloads produce editable PowerPoint charts and a real PDF instead of the print dialog.
decisions.why: Clients edit and present the packs.

decisions.title: Poppins everywhere
decisions.decision: Poppins in the site, PowerPoint and embedded in PDFs.
decisions.why: Brand consistency.

decisions.title: Consulting-grade pack structure
decisions.decision: Action titles, question chips, so-what boxes, Q&A, conclusions and method, based on your sample decks.
decisions.why: Packs must read like a strategy consultancy's work.

decisions.title: Automatic checks and self-correction for packs
decisions.decision: Server reviews each pack (lengths, numbers, missing parts) and the AI fixes issues once before publishing.
decisions.why: Stop layout and quality slips without manual review.

decisions.title: Route questions to the cheapest capable model
decisions.decision: Quick / balanced / deep tiers with automatic escalation, prompt caching and cost logged per answer.
decisions.why: Keeps the cost per answer low while reports stay high quality.

decisions.title: Client accounts with PIN login and plans
decisions.decision: Accounts, PINs (hashed), Junior/Senior/Owner limits, usage rings, chat history panel, pinned live dashboards.
decisions.why: Turns the demo into a sellable subscription.

decisions.title: Two pack versions
decisions.decision: A 5-slide executive brief and the ~12-slide full pack.
decisions.why: Executives read less; analysts want detail.

decisions.title: Job automation becomes one use case
decisions.decision: The platform is multi-use-case analytics; the job automation idea moves to use cases and proofs of concept.
decisions.why: Same engine serves many markets.

decisions.title: Lead with 'your own AI data analyst'
decisions.decision: The landing page opens with the personal AI analyst / data scientist, then use cases.
decisions.why: Clear value before examples.

decisions.title: Scrappa as second data provider, one schema per dataset
decisions.decision: Add Scrappa sources, each dataset in its own schema with analyst views.
decisions.why: Many SA datasets from one API; schemas keep them separate and safe.

decisions.title: No consumer property website
decisions.decision: Declined the idea of a public site where people browse properties.
decisions.why: Competes with portals that supply the data, licensing and POPIA risk.

decisions.title: POPIA by design
decisions.decision: No agent or seller personal data stored; PINs hashed; admin, CRM and client data never public.
decisions.why: Legal compliance and client trust.

decisions.title: Separate analysts sold as separate subscriptions
decisions.decision: Talent, Property, Retail Pricing and Marketplace analysts, each with its own data, skills, briefs and dashboards.
decisions.why: Each industry buys only what it needs.

decisions.title: Test new sources with few credits, then cap each source
decisions.decision: Probe each Scrappa source cheaply; a shared 25,000-credit monthly budget with caps per source.
decisions.why: Avoid burning credits on sources that don't work for SA.

decisions.title: Five expert skills per analyst
decisions.decision: Each analyst has five industry methods (e.g. CMA, rental yield screen, price-cut watch).
decisions.why: Clients pay for expert method, not just charts.

decisions.title: Track changes day to day
decisions.decision: Daily snapshots and 'what changed' views for listings, prices, jobs, salaries and ratings.
decisions.why: Trends need history; the source data only shows today.

decisions.title: Secrets only in GitHub Secrets and Render
decisions.decision: Keys never in chat or code; a token pasted in chat must be rotated.
decisions.why: A pasted admin token is exposed.

decisions.title: Lowest-cost production setup
decisions.decision: A .co.za domain, Zoho Mail free, Cloudflare DNS and Pages, Render Starter, stay on Neon free for now (~R300–R600/month fixed).
decisions.why: Keeps fixed costs low until clients arrive.

decisions.title: Deepen datasets with tools we already have
decisions.decision: Property24, Google Trends, unit prices, house brands and bigger volumes before adding new providers.
decisions.why: Use what is already paid for.

decisions.title: Clients bring their own data, isolated by the database
decisions.decision: CSV/Excel upload and Google Sheets first; each client gets a private schema and login that only it can read.
decisions.why: Clients want their numbers next to the market; isolation must not depend on app code alone.
decisions.alternatives: Shared tables with an account column; Sage connector first.

decisions.title: Live client connectors wait for a client
decisions.decision: No live connectors (Sage, ERP) until a paying client needs one.
decisions.why: Avoid building for imagined requirements.

decisions.title: Monthly report packs per analyst, with an honest look-back
decisions.decision: A pack on the 1st of every month, a Reports & dashboards page and landing cards; the 5-month look-back uses only real history (12-month search trends) and says where data starts.
decisions.why: Recurring value and promo content, without inventing history.

decisions.title: Production hardening of reports
decisions.decision: Prefer IPv4 on Render, re-apply database logins after setup, write reports one at a time.
decisions.why: Fixes found in the first runs (no IPv6 route, Neon login lock-out, memory).

decisions.title: Annotated charts that pop
decisions.decision: Charts mark anomalies, events, periods and ranges; stronger insight standard.
decisions.why: Readers should see the story without hunting.

decisions.title: Dark and alternating slide styles with raised tiles
decisions.decision: Light, dark and alternating dark / soft-green slides; rounded raised tiles; fill white space with insights.
decisions.why: Your preference, and a more premium look.

decisions.title: Admin brands each client's packs
decisions.decision: Logo, colours, cover image and style per client, applied automatically.
decisions.why: White-label value for agencies and brands.

decisions.title: Story reports as the base for social and video content
decisions.decision: A picture-led, plain-language Story deck next to the formal packs.
decisions.why: Engages everyday readers and feeds promo content.

decisions.title: Image library from an OpenRouter image model
decisions.decision: Generate ~50 tagged report images with an API image model, not a logged-in ChatGPT account.
decisions.why: A personal ChatGPT login can't be automated safely; the API is repeatable and logged.
decisions.alternatives: ChatGPT web app; stock photo licences.

decisions.title: A few custom image prompts per plan
decisions.decision: Clients can replace default pictures with their own prompts (proposed 10 / 40 / 200 a month).
decisions.why: Personalisation without runaway cost.
decisions.note: Needs the image key on Render.

decisions.title: A failed rewrite keeps the last good report
decisions.decision: Reports retry up to 3 times and never wipe a published report.
decisions.why: A restart had erased the Talent report.

decisions.title: Key insights that follow dashboard filters
decisions.decision: Insights recompute for the filtered view, default this month, with an Ask Acolyte AI bar about the current view.
decisions.why: Answers in context, without writing a question from scratch.

decisions.title: Expert depth explained in plain words
decisions.decision: Use expert models and explain each term and why it matters, documentary style, without dropping the analysis.
decisions.why: Readers range from executives to everyday people.

decisions.title: Web sources are quoted and checked
decisions.decision: Creative reports research the web and quote sources; the server drops any source the search didn't return.
decisions.why: Outside context helps, invented citations destroy trust.

decisions.title: Users choose the creative range
decisions.decision: Formal, Balanced or Creative style for answers.
decisions.why: Different readers and uses (board vs social).

decisions.title: Hide AI model names from users
decisions.decision: Choices read 'Thinking: Auto / Quick / Balanced / Deep'.
decisions.why: Customers buy an analyst, not a model.

decisions.title: Keep a decision register
decisions.decision: Record every product, design and technical decision with a timestamp, who made it and the effort it represents.
decisions.why: A shared memory of why things are the way they are.

decisions.title: Clients never see technical errors
decisions.decision: When the AI service fails, clients see a short message with a support reference; the full cause goes to the server log, the alerts and the owner only.
decisions.why: A raw billing error was shown in Ask AI; it exposes internals and looks broken.

decisions.title: Owner alerts by GitHub issue, every 10% of credit used
decisions.decision: Record each top-up (US$100 on 14 Nov); an hourly check opens a GitHub issue, which GitHub emails, at every 10% of the top-up used and at once if the credit runs out.
decisions.why: The Anthropic balance can't be read by the app, so spend since the top-up is tracked from Acolyte's own cost log.
decisions.alternatives: A fixed dollar threshold; checking the Console by hand.
decisions.note: Changed from a single $39 threshold to 10% steps at your request.

decisions.title: Our own sales CRM, built into the platform
decisions.decision: Replace the old local CRM (job-ad automation pitches) with a CRM for selling the industry analysts: prospects ranked from our own datasets, a pipeline board, notes, activity log and AI email drafts.
decisions.why: The data that powers each analyst also shows who needs it most; the old CRM needed a server on your computer.
decisions.alternatives: Keep the local CRM; buy HubSpot or Pipedrive.
decisions.note: Supersedes the job-automation CRM from 13 Nov.

decisions.title: Rank prospects by what each analyst can prove to them
decisions.decision: Agencies by stock, spread, price-cut pressure and new listings; retailers by basket coverage and price position; SA online stores by catalogue overlap, price position and reviews; employers and recruiters by hiring volume and employer rating.
decisions.why: Every reason in a pitch is a real number from our data, which makes the first email credible.
decisions.alternatives: Buy lead lists; rank by company size only.
decisions.note: Foreign online stores excluded from the marketplace list.

decisions.title: CRM in a private sales schema on Neon
decisions.decision: Prospects, activities and opt-outs live in their own schema, readable only with the admin key; the AI analyst and clients cannot see it. Prospects are businesses; contacts are added by you from business sources, and opt-outs block drafting.
decisions.why: POPIA and keeping sales data out of the public site and the analyst's reach.
decisions.alternatives: Store CRM data in the analyst schema.

decisions.title: The platform runs the sales funnel and assigns leads to account agents
decisions.decision: Hourly: assign top prospects to agents (least-loaded, within each agent's limit and the analysts they sell), draft emails into an Outbox, send approved ones, close leads with no reply, and email agents their new leads and tasks. Agents sign in with their own PIN and see only their leads.
decisions.why: Scale outreach without the owner doing every step, while keeping a person accountable for each lead.
decisions.alternatives: Owner works every lead by hand.
decisions.note: Starts with approval required before any email goes out; auto-send is a switch.

decisions.title: One permission email, then only with a yes (POPIA s69)
decisions.decision: The funnel sends at most one unsolicited email per contact, asking whether we may send our monthly report. The pack and follow-ups go only after a yes; no reply in 14 days closes the lead; opt-outs block everything.
decisions.why: POPIA s69 allows one approach to request consent for electronic direct marketing; every reputable email provider also bans cold email.

decisions.title: Brevo recommended over ZeptoMail; outreach from a real mailbox
decisions.decision: System email (assignments, tasks, alerts) via Brevo or ZeptoMail over HTTPS; email to people who said yes via Brevo; the single permission email 1:1 from a sales mailbox (Zoho Mail SMTP), or from the agent's own mail app until one is set up.
decisions.why: ZeptoMail's terms allow transactional email only, and it blocks marketing sends; Brevo allows email to people who opted in and covers both uses on one account.
decisions.note: You asked to use ZeptoMail, then said a better service was fine.
